2. The brief contents of the petition are as under:
On 23.10.2021 at about 10.00 pm., when the petitioner was travelling in a bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B- 9051 from Vokkaligara Samudhaya Bhavana S.S.Ghati Tobagere Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk near Happy Valley resorts, the driver of the bus drove the same with a very high speed, recklessness and suddenly dashed to the road safety guard at right side bus fell down.
Due to said impact, the petitioner and other passengers were forcibly knocked down and were sustained multiple grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital Doddaballapura wherein she took treatment as an inpatient for more than 6 days and spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards her SCCH - 09 3 MVC No.129/2022 treatment and nourishment.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

The accident in question occurred due to the rash and negligent manner of driving of Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06- B-9051 by its driver and the jurisdictional Doddaballapura Rural police have registered a case in their crime No.287/2021, after investigation the said police have filed a charge sheet against the said driver,
punishable under Section 279, 338 & 304(A) of IPC.
The first respondent being the insurer and the second respondent being the owner of said Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, on all these grounds, the petitioner prayed to allow this petition and award compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- under all heads together with interest and costs.

3. In response to the Court notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their SCCH - 09 4 MVC No.129/2022 counsel and respondent No.1 and 2 have filed their respective written statement.
4.
The brief contentions of the written statement of respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
Respondent denied the place, date and time of alleged accident and also denied the income and avocation of the petitioner.

Respondent contended that,
compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant. Further denied the involvement of Bus bearing No.KA-06- B-9051 in the alleged accident.
Further contended that, driver of the Bus was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Further contended that, the said Bus bearing reg.No.KA-060B-9051 was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.

Further the respondent No.1 has contended that, the owner of the vehicle and the concerned police have not SCCH - 09 5 MVC No.129/2022 complied the mandatory Manjula vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 19 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109424002/
2 provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.

The brief contentions of the written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 23.10.2022 at about 10.00 pm., the petitioner was travelling in a bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 in order to attend marriage reception and after completion of reception while returning back in the same bus near happy Valley Resorts, S.S.Ghati, Makalidurga Road, Doddaballapur Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, at that time the driver of the bus in which he was travelling drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly dashed to the road safety guard at right side bus fell down.
Due to impact the petitioner and other inmates of the said bus sustained grievous injuries in the alleged RTA ?

If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3.

the driver of the bus drove the same with a very high speed, recklessness and suddenly dashed to the road safety guard at right side bus fell down. Due to said impact, the petitioner and other passengers were forcibly knocked down and were sustained multiple grievous injuries.

10. To prove the accident that occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending bus, the petitioner herself got examined as PW-1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
On perusal of police document i.e., Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the charge sheet, Ex.P.4 is the spot panchanama, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report and Ex.P.6 is the sketch.

11. On perusal of documents, police have SCCH - 09 9 MVC No.129/2022 investigated the matter and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B- 9051 as per Ex.P.3 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338, 304(a) of IPC.
On perusal of said documents the owner and driver of the offending Bus have not disputed involvement of vehicles.
The respondent No.1 counsel suggested to the PW-1 that the said private bus was not having permit.

Therefore, by considering the oral and documentary evidence on record and above discussion, I am of the opinion that, the accident was occurred on negligence of driver of the offending Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.7, that document discloses the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, I answer the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into SCCH - 09 10 MVC No.129/2022 several facts like injuries, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant, charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., let me discuss one by one:
a) TOWARDS INJURY, PAIN AND SUFFERING:

The petitioner has contended that immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Government Hospital,
Doddaballapura wherein she took treatment and due to accident she sustained Manjula vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 19 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109424002/

In order to prove injuries caused to her she has produced wound certificate/Ex.P7, which reveals that, as per opinion of the doctor said injuries are grievous in nature. Further, Petitioner examined one Medical Record Technician as PW.2 and got marked Authrosiation letter, discharge summary, Clinical note, case diary, ECG and X-ray at Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.19.
Petitioner has also examined Dr.Manjunath.S.E. as PW.3 and got marked authorisation SCCH - 09 11 MVC No.129/2022 letter at Ex.P.20.
But PW.3 has not examined the petitioner to assess disability.

Therefore, by considering the avocation of the petitioner and as she sustained grievous injury as per Ex.P.7, it is just and proper to award the compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head pain and sufferings.

b) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES: The petitioner has produced out patient slip at Ex.P.12 and scan report marked at Ex.P.13 but not produced any medical bills to claim compensation towards medical expenses.

In the absence of relevant document,
petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards Medical Expenses.
c) TOWARDS FOOD, EXTRA NOURISHMENT, CONVEYANCE AND MEDICAL ATTENDANT CHARGES:

On perusal of records it came to know that, petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P.9, as per which she took treatment for implant removal and admitted for 3 days i.e., from 20.06.2022 to 22.06.2022 as an inpatient.
SCCH - 09 12 MVC No.129/2022 Petitioner also has examined medical record keeper working at Government Hospital, Doddaballapura and through him got marked Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.19.
Ex . P.15

is the discharge summary, on perusal of the same it came to know that, petitioner admitted to the said Government hospital from 23.10.2021 to 01.11.2021 for 10 days with a history of RTA and injury to the right clavicle, wherein she underwent procedure of ORIF with clavicle plate and screw.

In total, Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 13 days at the said Government Hospital,
Doddaballapura.

Considering the said fact, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 13 days and by including conveyance, in all a sum of Rs.15,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner contended that she was doing coolie work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In proof of the same, petitioner has not produced any document.

Therefore, in the absence of related document, to fix the income of the petitioner, lets rely on the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, which fixed notional income of the year 2021 at Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2021 treated as Rs.15,000/- p.m.,

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case this tribunal held that petitioner might have Manjula vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 19 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109424002/
5 taken two months rest.

sentences.text: Hence, petitioner is entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
e) TOWARDS FUTURE EARNINGS:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident she took treatment at Government Hospital.
Moreover, the petitioner has only examined the doctor as PW.3 who has not assessed the disability.
Therefore, the question does not arise to award under the head loss of future earning capacity.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled any compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
SCCH - 09 14 MVC No.129/2022  f) TOWARDS DEPRIVATION OF FUTURE AMENITIES:

The petitioner has contended that, on account of the said injuries, she has severe pain,
suffering from deep mental shock and agony, very dull due to the accident, cannot sit, squat, stand,
walk, climbing stairs and not bear weight etc.,
As per wound certificate she sustained grievous injury.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.40,000/- is just and reasonable towards under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
g) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Petitioner has not deposed with regard to the future medication therefore, she is not entitled for any compensation under the head future medical expenses.

sentences.text: Regarding Liability:
As already stated above the petitioner has proved that the accident in question was caused by the driver of the Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B- 9051 with rash and negligent act.
It is the contention of the respondent No.1 that, offending bus was not holding valid permit to ply on the road.
In support of the same, it has examined its Legal Executive as RW.1 and through him got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
On perusal of these documents it came to know that, the alleged offending bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 was not at all holding valid permit on the date of alleged accident.
SCCH - 09 16 MVC No.129/2022 Respondent No.2/Owner himself has examined as RW.2 and through him got marked 6 documents at Ex.R.4 to Ex.R.9.
During his cross examination, he has deposed that, -06--9051    .

Further deposed that,         
  ..   SCCH - 09 17 MVC No.129/2022       .
On perusal of said cross examination it can be come to the conclusion that, the offending bus bearing reg.No.KA- 06-B-9051 does not holding valid permit as on the date of alleged accident.

Therefore, lets rely on the citation reported in (2018) 8 Supreme Court Cases 492 (Rani and others Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others) wherein it is held that:
" Defence raised by insurer that offending vehicle did not possess a valid permit to operate in the State concerned - Accepting that defence, High Court absolving the insurer and fastening the liability on the insured i.e., the owner of offending vehicle directing him to satisfy the award - Held, even in such a case, the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle - Order of High Court modified accordingly".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

and others) wherein it is held that:
SCCH - 09 18 MVC No.129/2022 "The insurer, the first respondent herein, opposed the claim on the ground that, the vehicle in question was driven in violation of the terms of the insurance policy and further the driver was not having a valid and effective driving license and, therefore, it was not obliged to indemnify the insured.

On behalf of the owner of the vehicle and driver, assertions were made that the vehicle was insured with the first respondent as per the insurance policy, that the Manjula vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 19 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109424002/
7 vehicle was registered and the driver had the requisite driving licence.

sentences.text: Additionally, copy of the route permit of the offending truck was brought on record."

On perusal of above said discussion at citations it came to be know that, the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the owner are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.1 Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the SCCH - 09 19 MVC No.129/2022 compensation amount with interest to the petitioner at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.2.

The respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order and the petitioner is entitled for 6% interest on the compensation amount of .1,25,000/- from the date of petition till realisation.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of .1,25,000/- (Rupees one lakh twenty five thousand only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 - Insurer shall SCCH - 09 20 MVC No.129/2022 pay the compensation amount with interest at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.2 - Owner.
The respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, the entire amount with accrued interest shall be released on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.1 Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the SCCH - 09 19 MVC No.129/2022 compensation amount with interest to the petitioner at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.2.

13. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl
The respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order and the petitioner is entitled for 6% interest on the compensation amount of .1,25,000/- from the date of petition till realisation.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.3:
In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of .1,25,000/- (Rupees one lakh twenty five thousand only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 - Insurer shall SCCH - 09 20 MVC No.129/2022 pay the compensation amount with interest at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.2 - Owner.
The respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, the entire amount with accrued interest shall be released on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
